after.title: [MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS (part 1)
verificationCriteria: Given the Contentstack client is mocked to signal a draft entry change for the MX Homepage, the rendered Homepage shows the draft entry content instead of the previously published content, without requiring a full page reload.

Given the Contentstack client is mocked to signal a draft entry change for a Discover Article page, the rendered Discover Article page shows the draft entry content instead of the previously published content, without requiring a full page reload.
When no preview signal is active, the MX Homepage renders published content identically to its current behavior with no visual or functional regression.
When no preview signal is active, Discover Article pages render published content identically to their current behavior with no visual or functional regression.

Given the Contentstack client is mocked to signal multiple successive draft entry changes for the same Homepage, the rendered Homepage updates to reflect each change in sequence without a full page reload.

Given the Contentstack client is mocked to signal a draft entry change while the page is in a protected or gated state, the page does not render the draft content and continues to show the published content unchanged.

notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist in the codebase. The options object in contentstack.ts has no live_preview block, _app.tsx has no live-preview-utils initialization, and ContentstackContext is static (set once from SSR, never updated client-side). Attachment points are the SDK config, the app-wide provider, the React context, and the existing server-side fetch pattern to reuse for client-side re-fetching. VCs are derived from the description since the AC ('See in:') carries no testable content.

notes: Openspec's output contained only the placeholder 'See in:' with no testable criteria, so I built all ACs from scratch after reading the 8 listed files. Key observations from the codebase that shaped the ACs: (1) contentstack.ts options object has no live_preview block — AC 1 addresses this; (2) _app.tsx has no live-preview-utils initialization — AC 2 addresses this; (3) ContentstackContext is a static createContext with no update mechanism — ACs 6 and 13 address the need for dynamic updates; (4) useContent hook only reads, never writes — AC 13 addresses this; (5) Homepage receives page as props from SSR — AC 4 covers preview re-rendering; (6) No INewsArticlePage rendering path was visible but the interface exists — AC 5 covers Discover Articles; (7) The story's original notes mention protected pages limitation — AC 8 captures this explicitly; (8) No live-preview code exists anywhere in the codebase (searched for live_preview, livePreview, live-preview, ContentstackLivePreview, livePreviewUtils — zero matches). All ACs are phrased as observable outcomes (what a test can verify) with no implementation instructions per the WHAT-NOT-HOW rule.
